title: POC scoping: success criteria signoff - OmniHealth
summary: Redwood and OmniHealth agreed on explicit POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Main items: performance thresholds (latency & throughput), quality coverage (50-100 prompt sets, pass rates), data/security checks (audit logs, KMS), and reporting format (weekly benchmark sheet + final report). Timeline: 4-week POC with a mid-point benchmark run at week 2 and final sign-off at week 4. Action items and owners assigned for SOW/pricing, benchmark dataset delivery, and security review package.
action_items: Alex Morgan | Send draft SOW and pricing sheet | 2025-12-18
Ben Chu | Share representative prompt set (50-100 samples) and traffic profile | 2025-12-17
Priya Shah | Prepare benchmark harness and run initial dry-run on Redwood Dedicated | 2025-12-22
Maya Singh | Review security_pack_v2.pdf and confirm KMS/HSM requirements | 2025-12-20
next_steps: Redwood to send draft SOW + pricing (Alex)
Customer to provide prompt set and sample traffic profile (Ben)
Kickoff POC run and schedule week-2 benchmark (Priya/Alex)
Security review follow-up meeting to confirm VPC/KMS details (Maya & Redwood security)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we want to lock the success criteria for the OmniHealth POC today. um, quick rolL call, who's on from OmniHealth?
[00:12] Lisa Torres: Hi Alex, Lisa here, Ben and Maya on the call as well. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:20] Alex Morgan: Great, quick agenda: agreement on go/no-go thresholds, workload sizing, benchmark sheet and reporting format, and timelines. Priya from our SE team will talk mapping the benchmarks.
[00:35] Priya Shah: hi, hi, thanks. so uh I will run through the proposed acceptance tests — we have a template but we'll adapt to your app.
[00:45] Ben Chu: quick context — our main use case is clinical triage summarization and redaction, roughly 200 concurrent users at peak, about 1.5k requests per hour, low latency needed for the triage UI.
[00:58] Alex Morgan: OK, so two buckets: interactive triage (latency sensitive) and batch summarization (throughput). For the interactive path we're proposing p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms for text-gen endpoints on your workload profile. does that sound realistic?
[01:18] Ben Chu: p95 < 800ms might be tight depending on model size, but for the smaller curated model variant that should be fine. we're open to dedicated or hosted but prefer dedicated for data isolation.
[01:32] Maya Singh: security question — we need SOC2 level logs, KMS integration for key wrapping, and retention controls. also can you provide audit logs for inference requests?
[01:42] Priya Shah: yes, we provide per-request audit logs and we can integrate customer-managed KMS, we also have private deployment options if you need VPC/on-prem. note: sometimes the transcript will mis-say our product names, we call it Redwood Dedicated, but in some notes you see Redwood Dedicat or Orien, sorry.
[01:58] Lisa Torres: right, and for quality acceptance — we'd like human eval on a sample set. proposal: 100 prompts for the triage flow, 90% pass on clinical correctness + redaction accuracy (no PHI leakage). if lower, then fail.
[02:14] Alex Morgan: ok proposed quality thresholds: for summarization correctness, 90% pass rate on the sample set judged by your SMEs; for redaction, zero critical PHI misses on the 100-sample check. for embeddings/retrieval use-case, cosine similarity drop less than 0.03 compared to baseline.
[02:33] Ben Chu: sounds reasonable. what's the benchmark harness output format? we want token-level cost, latency percentiles, and per-route error rates.
[02:42] Priya Shah: we'll share a Google sheet benchmark_sheet.xlsx link — it includes tabs: latency (p50/p90/p95), throughput (RPS), cost breakdown (tokens, estimated $), quality pass/fail, and logs for sample traces. weekly snapshots and a final consolidated PDF.
[03:00] Lisa Torres: can you include a sample report format? our compliance team wants a change log and signed acceptance.
[03:07] Alex Morgan: yes we'll include an acceptance report template with signatures and a checklist. the go/no-go is explicit: all must pass (1) performance thresholds (p95), (2) quality thresholds, (3) security checklist. any critical fail means POC remediation period — we can run a second pass after tuning.
[03:24] Ben Chu: about workload sizing — I shared earlier a traffic profile but we'll formalize: peak concurrency 200, typical qps 15, sustained batch windows overnight with 100k tokens per hour.
[03:36] Priya Shah: that maps to a recommended instance plan on Redwood Dedicated: initial reserved pool with autoscale to burst for nightly batch jobs. we'll propose config in the SOW. note: we might recommend quantized model variants to reduce cost while keeping quality.
[03:51] Maya Singh: latency SLOs are important — what's the expected network overhead if hosted vs dedicated in our eu-west-1 region?
[03:59] Priya Shah: hosted routes go through public regions so additional egress lat, with dedicated in your VPC we can keep single-digit ms network inside region. we'll include region-specific numbers in the benchmark run.
[04:12] Lisa Torres: timeline — we'd like to start the POC next week if possible, 4 weeks total with week-2 interim benchmark. is that OK?
[04:20] Alex Morgan: yes proposed timeline: week 0 (kickoff + dataset exchange), week 1 (dry-run), week 2 (interim benchmark + tuning), week 3 (full run), week 4 (final report + sign-off). total ~4 weeks.
[04:33] Ben Chu: for the acceptance tests, do you run the workload replay or do we run it from our infra?
[04:38] Priya Shah: both options — we can run replay from Redwood infra to measure end-to-end or you can run it from your staging to include network. we usually do both for completeness.
[04:48] Maya Singh: can you confirm encryption at rest for model cache and KV cache, and whether logs include any PII fields by default?
[04:56] Priya Shah: encryption at rest including KV cache is supported and logs are configurable — by default we redact PII, but we'll work with your compliance team on exact fields.
[05:05] Alex Morgan: ok let's capture the acceptance criteria succinctly here:
[05:10] Alex Morgan: Acceptance tests (GO criteria):
- "Performance": interactive route p50 < 200ms, p95 < 800ms on Redwood Dedicated (with your network profile), batch throughput achieves X tokens/hour (we'll calculate exact target from your traffic).
- "Quality": clinical summarization >= 90% pass rate on 100-sample human-eval, redaction zero critical misses.
- "Security": KMS integration verified, SOC2-style audit logs available, and VPC isolation validated if deployed private.
- "Cost": token-level cost within agreed budget envelope (TBD in SOW).
[05:46] Ben Chu: minor follow-up — what about model fallbacks in case of capacity issues? we don't want outages.
[05:51] Priya Shah: we have smart routing and fallback to lighter quantized variants; we'll show 'fallback policy' in the SOW and console control for auto-fallback thresholds.
[05:59] Lisa Torres: reporting format again — weekly Google sheet snapshots plus a final PDF with acceptance checklist, and raw logs for 30 days.
[06:07] Alex Morgan: good. i'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and the acceptance checklist right after the call.
[06:12] Ben Chu: and scheduling — we need the mid-point run to coincide with our SME availability (week 2).
[06:17] Alex Morgan: noted, we'll book that now.
[06:20] Maya Singh: one more on legal/procurement — our procurement wants a draft MSA and data processing addendum; can you send a redline?
[06:27] Alex Morgan: yes we'll include MSA draft with the SOW.
[06:30] Priya Shah: quick technical note — for the benchmark harness we'll capture per-token timings, KV cache hit rates, and memory footprints. sometimes transcripts show 'K V cash' — it's KV cache.
[06:40] Ben Chu: ok good. any blockers from your side Alex?
[06:44] Alex Morgan: none, just need your prompt set and traffic profile. we'll aim to share the SOW by 12/18.
[06:51] Lisa Torres: sounds good. if all goes well, we expect to decide on Dedicated procurement by end of January.
[06:58] Alex Morgan: recap of next steps: send SOW/pricing, customer sends datasets, Redwood runs dry-run and week-2 benchmark, security review to confirm KMS/VPC details.
[07:12] Alex Morgan: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[07:16] Lisa Torres: thanks. bye.
